title: Firstwatch field scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick handoff + field-runbook for firstwatch (early morning) — lightweight, ephemeral notes that I keep on my laptop. Use this when you inherit pager + need fast triage and short-term mitigations.

Quick summary (what I usually do first):
- Check major pagers: prom-alerts:HighLatency, model-serving-evictions, gpu-pool-degraded.
- Slack: #oncall, post brief status + ETA within 5m. 
- Check Redwood console first: per-route latency graphs + recent rollouts.
- If customer-impacting, escalate to SRE lead + set incident channel.

Common temproary fixes (do not treat as permanent):
1) Throttled burst causing latency spikes:
   - Temporarily scale dedicated workers: infra autoscale -> add 2 nodes to pool "dedicated-a" (ui path: Infra > Pools > dedicated-a > scale)
   - OR: curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/pools/dedicated-a/scale -d '{"delta":2}' (auth: svc-oncall)
   - After spike subsides, revert scale within 30–60 min and document in JIRA.

2) Model KV cache thrash / OOMs on serving-runtime:
   - Identify which model id is evicting: grep recent logs for "kv_cache_eviction" and look for model-name.
   - If single model hogging memory, move traffic to fallback variant: redirect policy in console -> route -> fallback-model (canary to 10% then 0).
   - If rollback of recent model rollout: revert to previous config in console or use api PATCH /deployments/<id>/rollback.

3) GPU node degraded + pod restarts:
   - Drain node: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
   - If crashloop due to nvcc errors, capture dmesg and GPU driver logs -> /var/log/nvidia*.
   - Short-term: move critical routes to region fallback (routing policy > route > region-fallback -> us-west-2).

Pager-handling checklist (5 min):
- Identify alert scope (single model / route / whole pool).
- Determine customer impact (SLA boundaries).
- Post initial message in #oncall and incident channel.
- Start mitigation (scale/redirect/drain) and note actions in this doc.
- If not resolved in 15m, call SRE lead; open JIRA incident with summary template.

Things I like to jot during handoff: (copy this block into Slack DM)
- Active pagers: [names]
- Primary hypothesis: e.g., "kv-cache thrash from recent rollout of gpt-medium-v2"
- Actions taken: scale + redirect + node drain
- ETA for next update: +10m
- Next oncall: @name (time range)

Known recurring noisy alerts (short notes):
- prometheus:CPUThrottling often fires on testing workers around 03:00 UTC; usually safe to ignore if no capacity loss. Tag: "noisy" in alert.
- model-serving-evictions: happens after canary with new tokenizer; check recent PRs for tokenizer changes.

Unresolved/Risky items to raise later:
- Need permanent guardrails for rapid canary rollbacks (I keep reverting manually — tech debt).
- Batch autoscale thresholds too aggressive for bursty inference workloads.
- Better visibility into per-customer token consumption per route (improves root cause).

On-call quick commands (save these in your shell alias file):
- tail combined logs: 
  stern serving-runtime -n prod --include-container="inference"
- search kv evictions: 
  stern serving-runtime -n prod | grep -i "kv_cache_eviction" | tail -n 200
- scale pool: curl -X POST $INFRA_API/pools/<pool>/scale -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"delta":2}'

Draft runbook edits I want to make (add to Confluence later):
- Add a short checklist for "model rollback" with exact API endpoints and required approvals (currently manual).
- Document region-fallback costs and when to choose route redirection vs node scale.
- Paint a diagram of traffic flow when prefix-caching is enabled (helps oncall reason about cache misses).

Notes to self:
- Don't forget to label temporary scale actions with tag "firstwatch-temp" so billing team can filter.
- If you touch KMS keys for Private deployments, notify security (process: sec@redwood.com).

Open questions (for retrospective):
- How often should we automatically silence noisy non-actionable CPUThrottling alerts during early morning maintenance window?
- Can we add a single-click rollback button in the Console for common model rollbacks?

End-of-shift handoff template (copy into the handoff message):
- Summary of state (2 lines)
- Active pagers + current status
- Actions taken + where I left them (scales, drains, redirects)
- Pending tasks for next oncall (link to JIRA if open)
- Any recommended immediate follow-ups

TODOs: 
- Turn this scratchpad into a short Confluence page (task created: CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Add exact API curl examples with tokens redacted.

Random reminders: 
- Bring backups of ssh keys for edge clusters when coming into office.
- Check Maya's note about the new rollout schedule before 02:00 UTC.

-- Ravi (firstwatch)
